text.p: Hansapank and Hoiupank fell on the Tallinn bourse on Tuesday on profit-taking after a record-smashing bull run, but Tallinna and Uhispank gained, dealers said.
Trade was very active at 161.8 million kroons and the index fell 1.12 percent to 342.25.
Hansapank fell 5.12 kroons to 192.88 and Hoiupank fell 3.70 kroons to 196.50. Dealers said Hansa and Hoiu are expected to fall further on Wednesday.
"Investors took their short-term profits out and the market is waiting for further falls to take new positions," a dealer said.
Uhispank rose 2.35 kroons to 64.25 kroons and Tallinna Pank was 2.40 kroons higher to 66.40 kroons.
Dealers said the stocks were cheap compared to other leading banking shares. Uhispank was also buoyed by high foreign demand.
On the free market, Norma turned over 8.5 million kroons to close 1.50 kroons higher at 86.50.
Four new shares debuted on the bourse on Tuesday with fish producer Viru Rand on the free market being most active with 1.47 million kroons traded.
Construction company Merko on the main list was also active with almost one million kroons traded and its price rose to 118 kroons, slightly up from its OTC price, dealers said.
